subject: Inference economics: follow-up, budgets, and SLO choices
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: quick recap + next steps on pricing & SLOs

Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of what I heard
- Workload: user-facing product search + personalization, typical prompt lengths ~40-120 tokens, occasional long-form merchandising copy (~600 tokens) for batch jobs.
- Expected request profile: 75% short interactive calls, 25% batch generation during off-peak.
- Monthly volume ballpark: 200M–1.2B tokens (you gave a range, we used both low/mid/high scenarios).
- Primary constraint: want p95 latency under 500ms for interactive search; budgetary target is focused on $/1M-token economics.

Concrete asks I promised
1) Show rough unit economics for three options (Hosted standard, Hosted with streaming, Dedicated reserved capacity) and the trade-offs for latency vs $/1M tokens. See attached pricing calc.
2) Clarify SLO-driven pricing models and what we recommend for a pilot (we sketched 2 SLO tiers below).
3) Schedule a technical follow-up with Vivek to validate batching/streaming impact and measure p95 on a sample prompt set.

High-level recommendations (starter plan)
- Pilot: Hosted with streaming enabled for interactive traffic, conservative batching for batch jobs. This gives low tail latency while keeping unit cost moderate.
- If you need predictable unit cost and sustained throughput, Dedicated reserved (quarterly commit) reduces $/1M significantly but increases swapping and uptime coordination.

Proposed SLO tiers (for quoting):
- Tier A (Low-latency): p50 ~60–120ms, p95 <= 300–400ms (streaming + reserved capacity or larger hosted tier).
- Tier B (Cost-optimized): p50 ~120–250ms, p95 <= 800ms (aggressive batching, prefix caching, quantized model).

Next steps
- I attached a short pricing workbook with three scenarios. Please flag which monthly volume bucket you want me to price exactly (200M / 500M / 1B).
- Can we book a 45-min technical deep-dive with Vivek and your infra lead? I have windows Wed/Fri morning PT.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_calc.xlsx, SLO-options-summary.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm the preferred volume bucket.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0124
From: Alex Torres <atorres@acmeretail.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: quick recap + next steps on pricing & SLOs

Thanks Jonas — that looks good and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: leaning toward starting with a conservative 500M tokens/mo estimate for year 1 (growth expected). For budgeting, we want a modeled midpoint and an upside case at 1B.
2) Budget: procurement has given a target range of $40k–$75k/month all-in for the model inference line item (not including app infra). Roughly translates to a target of ~$50–$150 per 1M tokens depending on feature mix — we realize this is broad.
3) Latency: our product team insists on p95 <= 500ms for interactive search. We can accept slightly higher p50 if p95 is within target.

Questions for you:
- Can you surface an expected $/1M tokens for the two SLO tiers you proposed (Tier A and Tier B) at 500M and 1B volumes?
- For streaming: what's the expected delta in $/1M tokens vs non-streaming hosted for short prompts (40–120 tokens)?

Also looping Priya (infra) for scheduling the technical deep-dive — Priya, do Wed 10–11am PT work for you?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Product — Acme Retail
atorres@acmeretail.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: quick recap + next steps on pricing & SLOs

Appreciate the extra color — useful. Short answers here, and I attached a one-pager that maps the SLO tiers to ballpark unit economics.

Quick numbers (ballpark, per 1M tokens):
- Hosted / standard (no streaming): Tier A: ~$220 / 1M at 500M volume; Tier B: ~$140 / 1M.
- Hosted / streaming enabled (interactive): Tier A: ~$260 / 1M at 500M; Tier B: ~$170 / 1M.
- Dedicated reserved (quarterly commit, steady traffic): Tier A: ~$95–120 / 1M at 500M; Tier B: ~$60–80 / 1M.

Notes on deltas: streaming adds a per-request overhead (more RPCs, less batching opportunity) which increases unit cost for short prompts — but it tightens p95 dramatically for interactive flows. Dedicated setups allow us to do larger micro-batching and more aggressive quantization which lowers $/1M.

Latency vs cost trade-off, simplified:
- If your priority is stable low-tails (p95 <= 500ms) for interactive search, the fastest path is Hosted + streaming on a higher performance tier or Dedicated with reserved GPUs. That increases unit cost 20–60% vs cost-optimized batching.
- If you can tolerate p95 ~700–800ms, batching + prefix caching will reduce cost materially (Tier B numbers above).

Recommended immediate pilots
1) 2-week streaming pilot on Hosted: we enable streaming for interactive endpoints and run your canonical prompts against p95 SLAs. Goal: confirm p95 and measure real unit cost.
2) Parallel Dedicated sizing exercise: Vivek will propose node counts and expected cost curve if you choose to commit.

Vivek — can you prepare a short micro-benchmark plan (3 canonical short prompts, 1 long prompt) and an estimated node configuration for a 500M token/month profile?

Alex/Priya — Wed 10–11am PT works for us; I’ll drop a calendar invite.

Attachment: acme_mutual_action_plan.docx

—Jonas
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: quick recap + next steps on pricing & SLOs

Hi Priya / Alex — high level bench plan below. I'll bring raw numbers to the call.

Planned micro-bench (45–60 minutes work)
- Tests: 3x short prompts (40–120 tokens), 1x long prompt (~600 tokens)
- Modes: Hosted (no streaming), Hosted (streaming), Dedicated (single node), Dedicated (2-node cluster)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, effective $/1M computed from our pricing model

Important scoping notes
- For streaming measurements we'll use real-world concurrency patterns you described (spikey, interactive); streaming will show lower p95 but slightly higher per-token cost in hosted.
- Batching sizes: we'll test a small set (1, 4, 12) to capture trade-offs.

Deliverables
- A short results slide with recommendations for which SLO tier to use for pilot and one recommended config for a 500M/month pilot.
- A short appendix showing sensitivity of $/1M to prompt length and batching size.

I’ll upload the micro-bench plan and initial scripts to the Drive link Jonas shared.

—Vivek
